sources.entry: FutureOS - One AI agent everywhere you work - terminal, desktop, mobile, and IM bots driven by a single Rust backend.

summary.one_liner: FutureOS is an open-source, local-first AI agent backed by a single Rust gRPC core that runs in a terminal UI, desktop app, mobile apps, CLI, and IM bots.
summary.what_it_does: The agent runs as one gRPC backend that the terminal UI, desktop GUI, mobile apps, CLI, and chat-bot channels all connect to, sharing sessions, memory, and skills. Tool safety is configurable: read, write, edit, and shell tools can be set to off, manual approval, or sandbox, with macOS Seatbelt, Linux Bubblewrap, and Windows restricted-token protection named as platform-dependent options. Models can be used via bring-your-own API keys for built-in or custom OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible providers through auth.json and models.json, or via a FutureOS hosted sign-in. The README also describes long-running "goal" control for runs of 24+ hours, scheduled recurring tasks, forkable JSONL session history, and 15+ built-in skills. A host mode lets the desktop backend run headless on a server, and a self-hostable relay is described for phone-to-desktop remote control with end-to-end encryption.
use_cases: run an AI coding or research agent from the terminal
control a desktop AI agent from a phone
use my own OpenAI or Anthropic API key with an AI agent
run long multi-day agent research jobs
sandbox agent shell and file access
fork and branch AI chat sessions
how_to_run: future config  (set up a model provider)
notable: One Rust gRPC agent shared across terminal, desktop, mobile, CLI, and IM bot surfaces
Configurable approval tiers (off/manual/sandbox) with OS-level sandboxing
Headless host mode for running the agent on a server over SSH
Self-hostable relay with end-to-end encrypted phone-to-desktop channel
Bring-your-own-key support via auth.json and models.json for custom providers
caveats: Sandbox availability and guarantees differ by platform, and the desktop defaults to Unrestricted (off), per the README
The auto approval tier and FutureOS hosted models require a FutureOS sign-in
TCP mode is opt-in and should not be exposed beyond a trusted interface
